example.question: Three parallel lines $AD$, $BE$ and $CF$ cut off equal segments on the transversal $AC$, so $|AB| = |BC|$. Prove that they cut off equal segments on any other transversal $DF$, so $|DE| = |EF|$.

steps.title: Given and to prove
steps.say: Write down what you are given and what you must show, with a diagram.

steps.title: Draw two parallels
steps.say: Draw through $A$ a line parallel to $DE$. It meets $BE$ at $E'$ and $CF$ at $F'$. Draw through $F'$ a line parallel to $AB$, meeting $BE$ at $B'$.

lines.text: Construction: $AF' \parallel DE$, and $F'B' \parallel AB$ meeting $BE$ at $B'$.

steps.title: Make a parallelogram
steps.say: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, so $BCF'B'$ is a parallelogram. Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal.

steps.title: Prove two triangles congruent
steps.say: Look at the triangles $ABE'$ and $F'B'E'$ that meet at $E'$. Find two equal angles and one equal side.

lines.text: So the triangles are congruent by **ASA**, and $|AE'| = |F'E'|$.

steps.title: Pass the equality to $DF$
steps.say: $AE'$ and $DE$ are opposite sides of a parallelogram, and so are $F'E'$ and $FE$.

example.question: In the triangle $ABC$, the line $XY$ is parallel to $BC$, with $X$ on $[AB]$ and $Y$ on $[AC]$. It cuts $[AB]$ in the ratio $|AX| : |XB| = 2 : 3$. Prove that $|AY| : |YC| = 2 : 3$.

steps.title: Given and to prove
steps.say: State the given, the claim, and draw the triangle with $XY \parallel BC$.

steps.title: Divide $[AB]$ into equal parts
steps.say: The ratio is $2 : 3$, so split $[AB]$ into $2 + 3 = 5$ equal parts. Two parts lie along $[AX]$ and three along $[XB]$.

lines.text: Each part has the same length, call it $m$.
Construction: through each point of division draw a line parallel to $BC$.

steps.title: Use Theorem 11
steps.say: The new lines are parallel and cut equal segments on the transversal $AB$. By Theorem 11 they cut equal segments on any other transversal, so also on $[AC]$.

lines.text: $[AC]$ is divided into 5 equal parts, 2 of them in $[AY]$ and 3 in $[YC]$.

steps.title: Compare lengths
steps.say: Let $k$ be the length of one part on $[AC]$. Then count parts in $[AY]$ and $[YC]$.

The key idea: fit a copy of the smaller triangle inside the larger, show the copy gives a **parallel** line, then use Theorem 12.

example.question: The triangles $ABC$ and $DEF$ are similar, with equal angles at $A$ and $D$, at $B$ and $E$, at $C$ and $F$. Prove that $\dfrac{|AB|}{|DE|} = \dfrac{|BC|}{|EF|} = \dfrac{|CA|}{|FD|}$.

steps.title: Given and to prove
steps.say: Write down the given, the claim, and draw both triangles.

lines.text: Given: triangles $ABC$ and $DEF$ with equal angles.

steps.title: Mark off the smaller triangle
steps.say: Place a copy of $DEF$ inside $ABC$. Put $E'$ on $[AB]$ with $|AE'| = |DE|$ and $F'$ on $[AC]$ with $|AF'| = |DF|$. Join $E'$ to $F'$.

lines.text: Construction: $E'$ on $[AB]$ with $|AE'| = |DE|$, and $F'$ on $[AC]$ with $|AF'| = |DF|$.

steps.title: Prove two triangles congruent
steps.say: $AE'F'$ and $DEF$ have two equal sides and the angle between them equal (the angle at $A$ equals the angle at $D$).

lines.text: $\triangle AE'F'$ is congruent to $\triangle DEF$. Reason: **SAS**.

steps.title: Show $E'F'$ is parallel to $BC$
steps.say: Congruent triangles have equal angles, so $|\angle AE'F'| = |\angle DEF| = |\angle ABC|$. These are corresponding angles.

steps.title: Use Theorem 12
steps.say: A line parallel to one side divides the other two sides in the same ratio.

lines.text: Repeat from the vertex $B$ to get $\dfrac{|AB|}{|DE|} = \dfrac{|BC|}{|EF|}$. Done.

example.question: In triangle $ABC$, $D$ is on $[AB]$ and $E$ is on $[AC]$ with $|\angle ADE| = |\angle ABC|$. Given $|AD| = 4$, $|DB| = 2$ and $|DE| = 5$, prove that triangles $ADE$ and $ABC$ are similar, and find $|BC|$.

steps.title: Read the diagram
steps.say: List what the diagram gives you and the claim to prove. Mark equal angles on it.

steps.title: Find a second equal angle
steps.say: Both triangles share the angle at $A$. It is the same angle in each, so it is equal.

steps.title: Name the third angle
steps.say: Angles in a triangle sum to $180^\circ$ (Theorem 4). Two angles equal means the third is equal.

lines.text: So $\triangle ADE$ and $\triangle ABC$ are **similar**: all three angles equal.

steps.title: Use proportional sides
steps.say: By Theorem 13, similar triangles have proportional sides. Match $DE$ with $BC$ and $AD$ with $AB$.
